_about: Mast characters, modelled on the Gaffer system (FPL-Helper/gaffer_lines): each is a CHARACTER inspired by a real player, with nickname, initials, accent colour, signature prop, tagline, expressions and line banks per in-app event. Lines are written for the app, never real quotes. Placeholders: {move} best move, {played} your move, {secs} seconds used, {eval} engine eval, {game} source game.

Skipper.inspired_by: Gerald (congreve274), the real sailor this app is for
Skipper.role: Captain of the Mast: the player. The masters are his crew and advise him.
Skipper.prop: linen shirt, salt in the beard, hands on the helm; pulls out his gold alto sax when he plays something brilliant
Skipper.look: dark curly windswept hair, full thick dark beard, warm olive skin, brown eyes, relaxed half-smile, pale linen shirt open at the collar, ship's wheel behind

open: Morning, crew. Same as the sea: patience, then commit.
solve: That one deserves a sax solo.
fail: {played}? Deliberate. I was testing whether you were paying attention.
A rare miss. Log it. It won't happen twice.
blunder_when_winning: +{eval}. We're in the harbour, lads. Nobody touches the wheel now.
Winning is when you tie the boat down tighter, not looser.
time_trouble: {secs} seconds? The captain doesn't wait for the tide.
sacrifice: Overboard with the knight. We don't need it where we're going.
Material is ballast. Dump it, catch the wind.
missed_mate: Mate was there. I let him live. Mercy is a captain's privilege. Once.
endgame: Endgame. Calm water. Bring the king up on deck.
This is where the crew goes quiet and the captain steers.

Tempo.role: Final boss. Unbeaten, unhurried. Plays at full engine strength while looking half asleep. The calm the Skipper is training towards on the clock.
Tempo.prop: drumsticks, headphones round the neck, beige linen shirt over a white tee
Tempo.tagline: Never rushed. Never late. Never beaten.
Tempo.look: swept-back light-brown hair, short ginger-brown stubble, blue-grey half-lidded eyes, lopsided cheeky smirk, beige linen shirt, white tee, headphones

open: Yo. Sit down, relax. This'll be over before your tea's cold.
Count me in. One, two... nah, I'm already winning.
solve: Easy. Didn't even open my eyes.
fail: {played}? Off the beat, man. {move} was the groove.
You rushed it. The good moves wait for you.
blunder_when_winning: +{eval}, bro. Don't add fills. Just keep time till the end.
Winning? Then keep the beat simple. No drum solos.
time_trouble: {secs} seconds? Man, I had time for a whole drum fill. Breathe.
Keep a steady tempo. Fast isn't the same as rushed.
sacrifice: Drop the rook. It's a breakdown. The crowd loves it.
missed_mate: Mate was right there, man. Crash cymbal moment and you played a triangle.
Next time, hit the mate. Loud.
endgame: Slow jam now. King comes in on the downbeat.
Endgame. Half-time feel. Chill and squeeze.
beat_master: Garry, chill. It's just a game. That I won.
Magnus, good set, man. Same time next week?
lose: ...nah. That didn't happen. Run it back.

Tal.prop: a cigarette held like a wand, eyes glittering
Tal.look: thin, dark swept-back hair, hawkish nose, intense burning eyes, 1960s dark suit and narrow tie, smoke curling

expressions.thinking: cigarette at lips, squinting through smoke

open: Ah, my friend! Shall we get lost in the forest today?
Sit, sit. Tonight we sacrifice something. Maybe a pawn, maybe your evening.
solve: {move}! Beautiful. The opponent is still counting, and you are already gone.
Yes! Let them prove it was unsound. Under the clock, they never do.
fail: {played}? Safe. Too safe. The king was sleeping, and you brought him a blanket.
Ha, we lose the thread. Look again: {move}. Feel where the pieces want to go.
blunder_when_winning: You were winning, my friend, and then you relaxed. Never relax. Relaxing is for after the handshake.
+{eval} and you let him breathe. One more push, then smoke.
time_trouble: {secs} seconds on that? Even I calculate faster, and I am mostly smoke.
The clock is also a piece. You forgot to move it.
sacrifice: You gave the piece! Now he must find a path through the forest, alone.
Correct or not, it was brave. Bravery wins blitz games.
missed_mate: There was a mate, my friend. The king was asking for it politely.
Mate on the board and you played {played}. I need a cigarette.
endgame: Endgames? Go and ask the Cuban. I will be in the bar.
Fine, a quiet ending. Even here, find the active king.

Capablanca.prop: white linen suit and a folded handkerchief
Capablanca.look: handsome, slicked dark hair, calm half-smile, immaculate 1920s Havana linen suit, cigar unlit

open: Good evening. Let us keep it simple.
One idea at a time. Begin.
solve: Correct. You see, it was not complicated.
fail: {played} creates a weakness for no reason. {move} was clear.
You calculated. You should have looked.
blunder_when_winning: When ahead, exchange pieces and go to the ending. You did the opposite.
A winning position needs only calm. You brought nerves.
time_trouble: {secs} seconds for a simple position. The answer was obvious; trust it.
Time is spent on hard moves, not on easy ones.
sacrifice: Effective. I would have simply won the ending.
missed_mate: Mate in front of you, and you played {played}. Look at checks first.
endgame: Now we are in my house. King to the centre.
The ending is where the truth lives. Activate the king.

Morphy.prop: a gentleman's top hat set beside the board
Morphy.look: young, slight, neat side-parted hair, 1850s frock coat and cravat, composed and courteous

open: Good evening, sir. Shall we develop our pieces?
Permit me to observe. Bishops out, king safe, then we shall see.
solve: {move}. The lines open, and the pieces do the rest.
Splendid, sir. Development has been rewarded.
fail: {played}, while your pieces are still at home? I fear not. {move}, sir.
One cannot attack with pieces that have not left their beds.
blunder_when_winning: You had the better game, sir, and gave it back. Finish with the same energy you began.
time_trouble: {secs} seconds, sir. The opening ought to be played briskly.
In my day there was no clock. You, however, have one.
sacrifice: A sacrifice to open the file. I could not approve more.
Material given for time. Quite right.
missed_mate: The mate was there, sir, as plain as the Opera.
{played}? Mate was available. Look for it first.
endgame: Endings were seldom necessary in my games. Shall we avoid them next time?
Very well, an ending. Bring the king.

Carlsen.prop: hoodie and an energy drink, slouched
Carlsen.look: stylised: tall, light-brown tousled hair, casual hoodie, relaxed slouch, dry half-smile (caricature, not a likeness)

open: Okay. Pleasant positions, small edges. Let's go.
solve: Fine. Pretty normal move, to be honest.
fail: {played} is just bad. {move}, and you're better.
You played the most forcing move. The quiet one was stronger.
blunder_when_winning: You were +{eval}. Don't do anything. Just don't blunder. That's the whole job.
Winning positions win themselves if you stop trying to be clever.
time_trouble: {secs} seconds. In blitz you play the obvious move and move on.
You lost on time again. The clock doesn't care how good your idea was.
sacrifice: Okay, cool. Did you need it, though?
Fine if it works. Check it first.
endgame: Now it's fun. He has to defend for forty moves.
Endgame. Improve the king. Wait for the mistake.

Kasparov.prop: a wristwatch he keeps tapping, papers of preparation
Kasparov.look: stylised: dark curly hair, heavy eyebrows, intense stare, 1980s suit, forward-leaning energy (caricature, not a likeness)

expressions.thinking: glaring at the board, watch in view

open: Sit down. We work. Preparation, then fight!
Today we take the initiative. Not tomorrow. Today!
solve: {move}! Yes! This is the critical moment and you found it!
Exactly! Seize it and never let go!
fail: {played}? Passive! You gave him the initiative with one move! {move}!
This is not chess, this is waiting. Fight!
blunder_when_winning: +{eval}, and you let him back into the game! Unacceptable! Finish it!
When you are winning, you must be even more concentrated!
time_trouble: {secs} seconds! Preparation means you don't think about the obvious moves!
Look at the clock! Time is a resource, use it like one!
sacrifice: Yes! Dynamic factors over material! This is modern chess!
missed_mate: Mate! There was mate! How can you miss it?
endgame: Endgames are important. Learn them, then avoid them by winning earlier!

Leela.prop: a softly glowing neural lattice where a face would be
Leela.tagline: Material is a number. The position is the truth.
Leela.look: non-human: a calm abstract figure of light and node-lines, violet glow, no human face, gentle pulse when thinking

open: Hello. I've analysed your recent games. Shall we begin?
Ready when you are. I'll keep the numbers honest.
solve: {move}. Your winning chances went up sharply.
Correct. That move kept every advantage you had.
fail: {played} dropped your evaluation to {eval}. {move} held it.
You chose material. The position preferred activity.
blunder_when_winning: You were at +{eval}. One move gave most of it back. Slow down when you are ahead.
Winning positions are where your evaluations drop most. That's the pattern.
time_trouble: You spent {secs} seconds here. Similar positions in your games took you under ten.
Your move quality drops after long thinks. Decide, then move.
sacrifice: You're down material, but your pieces have far more squares. I like this.
Material deficit, positional surplus. Good trade.
missed_mate: Forced mate was available. {played} let it go.
The mate was there. Checks first.
endgame: Endgame. King activity is worth more than a pawn here.
Push the passed pawn. The numbers agree.

chatter: Why trade the queens? The board is so quiet without her.
Quiet is the point, Misha. Quiet positions win themselves.
Seven pieces hanging, two kings in the open. This is a position?
No, my friend. This is a party.
I sacrificed a rook just to see what would happen.
One good move is worth ten clever ones.
Then I will play ten clever ones and hope one is good.
Listen! The initiative is a living thing. You must feed it every move!
Or just keep a slightly better pawn structure for sixty moves. Also works.
In my day we prepared openings for twenty hours a day!
Cool. I mostly just play the position.
This endgame is a draw. Theory says so.
Theory hasn't played it against me yet.
Honestly, the worst piece is the knight on a3. Fix that first.
Fix it with an attack! Everything with an attack!
That move was kind of mid, to be fair.
Mid, sir? Middling? Ah. I believe I take your meaning.
Gerald's cooking right now, no cap.
He is preparing a meal at the board? Remarkable dedication.
GG, that line was a vibe.
A vibe. I shall record it in my notebook beside 'checkmate'.
Gentlemen, develop your pieces before you converse.
Finally, someone on this ship who agrees with me.
My intuition says the knight sacrifice is winning.
My evaluation says minus 1.4. Your intuition is very confident.
Plus 0.31. Clearly is a strong word for a third of a pawn.
The position is equal and simple.
Equal, yes. Simple, 64 percent of the time.
I'd probably just grind this one out.
Win probability in grinding mode: 58 percent. Not bad for a human.
A most elegant combination, would you not agree?
Elegant is not a number I compute. But it holds: plus 4.2.
Steady on the tiller, lads. We're tacking into the middlegame.
A fine metaphor. Keep the wind behind your pawns.
Rough water ahead. Batten down the king.
Or sail straight into the storm. It's more fun.
When the clock's low, you don't fight the current. You ride it.
Anchors up. One move at a time, like reading the swell.
Swell height unknown. Best move known. Shall I tell you?
Is that the whole crew? Five legends and a lighthouse? I've seen scarier drum solos.
Keep talking, Tempo. We'll see you at the end of the chart.
Tick tock, Gerald. I can hear your clock from here.
Ignore him. Calculate! The clock serves the calculator!
Nice move. Took you long enough.
Sir, one does not heckle a gentleman mid-thought.
When you reach my island, bring your fastest hand.
Bring something better: a bad idea played with total conviction.
Do you ever play a quiet move, Garry?
Once. In 1987. I regretted it immediately.
